newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Austrian general to command U.N. Sahara operation.
newsitem.headline: Austrian general to command U.N. Sahara operation.

text.p: Brigadier-General Bernd Lubenik of Austria will take over command of the U.N. Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) on Aug. 1, the United Nations said on Monday.
Lubenik will succeed Major-General Jorge Barrosos de Moura of Portugal, who has held then post since Nov. 30, 1996.

MINURSO, comprising about 235 military observers and troops, was set up in September 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and organise a referendum to decide whether the former Spanish colony should be incorporated into Morocco, which controls most of the territory, or become independent, as called for by the Polisario Front.
The referendum, originally set for January 1992, has been repeatedly postponed because of disagreement over who should be eligible to vote.

Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker was appointed Secretary-General Kofi Annan's personal envoy for the Western Sahara in March. He has held talks with representatives of both sides to help determine whether the U.N. plan can still be implemented or some other solution must be found.
Baker reported some progress after talks in London earlier this month and said another round would be held Aug. 29-30 at a venue that has not yet been announced.
